questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: The stages of a European integration project
questions.stem: Why does European integration proceed in stages rather than all at once?

answer.exemplar: Staged integration lets members adjust gradually, builds trust through early wins and allows democratic ratification at each step, reducing the risk of rejection.

questions.explanation: Staged integration allows gradual adjustment, builds trust through early wins and permits democratic ratification. The tempting view sees only delay.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: The order of the European project

stimulus.body: The sequence ran from coal and steel pooling to a common market, then to European citizenship and a single currency. Each stage deepened ties while leaving national governments in place.

questions.stem: What stayed in place at each stage according to the passage?

options.text: All currencies were replaced at once
All national governments were abolished
All borders were erased immediately
National governments stayed in place at each stage

questions.explanation: National governments stayed in place at each stage. Abolition, erased borders and instant currency replacement are wrong.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A competence held only at the common level
questions.stem: Why are some competences held only at the common level?

options.text: Because national governments are always incompetent
Because common problems need uniform rules to work
Because local voters prefer common control
Because common level means no rules at all

questions.explanation: Common problems need uniform rules to work. National incompetence, voter preference and no rules are wrong.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A clause on external trade

stimulus.body: The clause gave the union exclusive power to negotiate trade deals with third countries, and required member states to align their external tariffs accordingly.

questions.stem: What did the clause require of member states?

options.text: It required them to leave the union
It required them to abolish all tariffs internally
It required them to align their external tariffs
It required them to ban all imports

questions.explanation: The clause required aligning external tariffs. Abolishing internal tariffs, leaving and banning imports are wrong.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: The bargain at a tariff round
questions.stem: What is exchanged at a tariff round?

options.text: Weather data is exchanged
Military bases are exchanged
Sports trophies are exchanged
Concessions on tariffs and subsidies are exchanged

questions.explanation: Tariff rounds exchange concessions on tariffs and subsidies. Bases, trophies and weather data are wrong.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: Consequences of removing a tariff

stimulus.body: After the tariff was removed, consumer prices dropped and imports surged. Domestic producers complained of unfair competition, while exporters in other sectors enjoyed cheaper inputs.

questions.stem: Which group benefited from cheaper inputs?

options.text: Domestic steel producers benefited from cheaper inputs
Exporters in other sectors benefited from cheaper inputs
Foreign governments benefited from cheaper inputs
options.misconception: introduces an actor absent from the text

options.text: No one benefited from cheaper inputs

questions.explanation: Exporters in other sectors benefited from cheaper inputs. Domestic producers complained, and foreign governments and no one are wrong.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A supply chain that creates dependency
questions.stem: How can a country reduce dependency created by a supply chain?

answer.exemplar: It can diversify suppliers, build domestic capacity, stockpile critical inputs and negotiate long-term contracts to reduce vulnerability to disruption.

questions.explanation: Diversifying suppliers, building capacity, stockpiling and contracting reduce vulnerability. The tempting view sees only trade bans.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A line that stops

stimulus.body: The new boundary on the map halted expansion of industrial zones into a protected wetland. Factories already operating could remain, but no new permits would be issued beyond the line.

questions.stem: What could still happen inside the existing zone?

options.text: New factories could be built freely
All existing factories had to close
Existing factories could remain and operate
The wetland was drained immediately
options.misconception: introduces an action absent from the text

questions.explanation: Existing factories could remain. Closing them, free new building and draining the wetland are wrong.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: Who gains inside one country
questions.stem: Which group typically gains from cheaper imports after a tariff cut?

options.text: No one gains from cheaper imports
Import-competing producers typically gain from cheaper imports
Only foreign governments gain
options.misconception: introduces an actor absent from the standard account

options.text: Consumers typically gain from cheaper imports

questions.explanation: Consumers typically gain from cheaper imports. Import-competing producers lose, and foreign governments and no one are wrong.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: Gains and losses in different places

stimulus.body: The study found that port cities grew faster after integration, while rural manufacturing regions stagnated. It recommended targeted investment to spread benefits more evenly.

questions.stem: What did the study recommend?

options.text: It recommended closing all ports
It recommended targeted investment to spread benefits
It recommended ending integration entirely
It recommended taxing only rural areas
options.misconception: introduces a policy absent from the text

questions.explanation: The study recommended targeted investment to spread benefits. Closing ports, ending integration and rural-only taxes are wrong.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A review of quotas and votes
questions.stem: Why might a review of quotas and votes be contentious?

answer.exemplar: Because changing voting weights redistributes power among members, so states that would lose influence resist while those that would gain support the change.

questions.explanation: Changing weights redistributes power, so losers resist and gainers support. The tempting view sees only technical adjustment.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: The quota rule behind the votes
questions.stem: What is the purpose of setting a quota for decisions?

options.text: The purpose is to prevent any decision ever
The purpose is to let one state decide everything
The purpose is to balance efficiency with protection of minority interests
The purpose is to abolish all voting

questions.explanation: A quota balances efficiency with protection of minority interests. One-state control, no decisions and abolishing voting are wrong.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A programme attached to a loan

stimulus.body: The programme required the borrower to reduce deficits, reform tax collection and open markets. Critics argued the pace was too fast and ignored local conditions, while supporters cited improved growth later.

questions.stem: What criticism did the programme face according to the passage?

options.text: It was criticised for having no conditions at all
It was criticised for being too slow and too local
It was criticised for abolishing all taxes
options.misconception: introduces a policy absent from the text

options.text: It was criticised for being too fast and ignoring local conditions

questions.explanation: The programme was criticised for being too fast and ignoring local conditions. Too slow and abolishing taxes are wrong.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: Conditions written into an agreement
questions.stem: What tension do loan conditions create for the borrower?

They create tension between policy autonomy and access to funds
They create tension between sports and education
They create no tension at all

questions.explanation: Loan conditions create tension between policy autonomy and access to funds. Weather, sports and no tension are wrong.
